title: feat(lint): warn when a full record page's header title or action order differs from what the phone and the drawer draw
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-sales"} -->
_Requested by **Sales** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4Uu?thread=cmsg_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4UuCaKzL3EuG5C8Gc9fbgPnaB)_

repo:objectstack#1 · os-sales · session_01L6bhgWrQDK4fwFgWf8ZrrR

Part of #36202 (the platform half; the card stays open until a HotCRM release carries its aligned pages and the three surfaces are rechecked, which the seat tracks)

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 最终用户无感；应用开发者在校验、构建或发布页面时，如果手写记录页的页头标题或按钮顺序和手机、预览上的不一致，会看到一条提示，发布照常进行。
- 属于记录页专题：同一条记录在电脑整页、右侧预览、手机上标题和主按钮不一样，这次按你选的「应用对齐，平台加发布提示」只加提示和说明。
- 出错最多是多一条或少一条提示，页面怎么显示完全不变；撤回只需删掉这条规则。
- 无。

## What changes

Per the maintainer ruling on #36202 (record 7072788648, 「应用对齐，平台加发布提示」): platform behaviour and the spec are unchanged; one advisory rule and its author docs are added.

An object's hand-written full record page (`type: 'record'`, `kind: 'full'`) is drawn on the desktop full page only; on a phone and in every embedded record view the record draws the standard page, built from the object. `validateRecordPageHeader` (`packages/lint/src/validate-record-page-header.ts`) names a full page's `page:header` that makes the same record read differently between the two:

- `record-page-header-title-differs`: a `title` that is not exactly the object's name field token (`{nameField}`, or the field `objectTitleCompleteness` derives). Every locale of an inline locale map is judged.
- `record-page-header-actions-differ`: the header's `actions` list, sorted the way the header renderer sorts (`order` ascending, then `variant: 'primary'`, then the incoming order; `headerActionPlan` in `ui/packages/components/src/renderers/layout/containers.tsx`), gives a different primary button, or a different order within the button row or within the overflow menu, than the object's placed actions sorted the same way with their declaration order as the incoming order (the standard page also draws placed actions the list leaves out). The primary is picked as the renderer picks it: the first non-destructive button declaring `variant: 'primary'`, else the first button.

Both are `warning`s, on every command and on the page publish door (`runtimeTypes: ['page']`), where they ride back on the 2xx `advisories` and refuse nothing. Wiring:

- `authoring-rules.ts`: one registry row (advisory, `CLI_AND_RUNTIME`), after `validateRecordTitle`.
- `validate-record-page-header.user-text.ts`: the Studio user's sentence for both ids in all 11 platform locales, merged in `finding-user-text.ts`.
- `rule-explanations.ts`: `os explain` text for both ids, including what the check cannot see.
- `index.ts`: the rule and its two id constants exported beside the record-title rule.
- `content/docs/ui/pages.mdx` (Where an authored page applies): where the title (object `nameField`) and the primary action and order (action `order` / `variant: 'primary'`) are declared, and that a header meant to differ everywhere belongs in a slotted page's `header` slot.
- `runtime-gate.page-visibility-predicate-writes.test.ts`: the page door's rule-list pin gains the new row in registry order.
- Four `os validate` / `os build` transcripts in `content/docs/` (`cli.mdx`, `validating-metadata.mdx`, `build-with-claude-code.mdx`, `react-pages.mdx`): the author-time rule count 74 → 75, which `check:docs-transcript-drift` derives from the registry.

What the static check does not catch (stated in the finding's message and in `os explain`): an action's `visible` / `enabled` predicates and permissions (it can name a difference the runtime hides, e.g. two actions with mutually exclusive visibility); actions another installed package attaches to the object; and the served declaration order, estimated as the object's own `actions` then the stack's `actions` bound by `objectName` in source order. A header naming an action the stack does not declare on the object is not judged, so at the publish door, whose `page` snapshot carries `objects` but not the stack-level `actions` collection, the action half judges only what the snapshot shows (it can be quieter there, never invent a finding). Print, slotted, html/react and non-record pages, and pages bound to no declared object, are not judged.

Small choices made in the thread: two rule ids rather than one (they have different fixes); the button row and the overflow menu are compared apart because they are drawn apart (an earlier draft compared one sequence and flagged the showcase's task page, whose two record_more-only actions are listed after its buttons, for an order nobody sees).

Skills-docs: none — Metadata-protocol is `none` and no arm is declared; any skills wording is a separate `domain:skills` card.

## Tests

- `packages/lint/src/validate-record-page-header.test.ts` (24 cases): both findings on the shipped lead shape; title omitted / exact token / derived field / locale map / nested header; primary and order arms; declared `order` and `variant: 'primary'` silencing it; an unlisted placed action leading the standard page; object-inline actions ahead of bound ones; destructive, menu-pinned and record_more-only actions never the primary; the button row and the overflow menu compared apart; unresolved ids and `placedActions` not judged; slotted, print, home, html, unbound and foreign-object pages not judged; the registry row; a page write through `runRuntimeAuthoringRules` returning the advisory with no error and a valid `userMessage`; the action half judging only what the snapshot shows; the user-text catalog in every platform locale rendered from real findings.
- Whole `@objectstack/lint` suite and typecheck on 9b06321b: see Verification.

## Acceptance notes

- HotCRM, run with this rule over each package stack of `objectstack.composition.ts` (the CLI's per-package pass) and over all packages together:
  - hotcrm `main` 6090c837: **0 findings** (its only full record pages left are the quote and contract print pages, not judged).
  - hotcrm `v6.5.0` 5d4ce04f: 3 findings: `lead_detail_page` title (`{full_name}` vs `display_title`), `lead_detail_page` primary (`qualify_lead` vs `convert_lead`), `case_detail_page` primary (`reopen_case` vs `escalate_case`). The two lead findings are exactly the card's observation (确认线索 on the full page, 转化线索 on the phone and drawer). The case one is the visibility limit above: the seat's review read reopen and the other two as mutually exclusive by visibility, so on a given record the primary is probably the same.
- In-repo: `examples/app-showcase` (objects, actions and pages) 0 findings; `examples/app-crm` 0; no platform record page declares a header `title` or an `actions` list (the user, organization and approval request pages use `placedActions: true`).

## Verification

- Two-minute check: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint exec vitest run src/validate-record-page-header.test.ts` → 24 passed.
- Files to read first: `packages/lint/src/validate-record-page-header.ts` (the two comparisons, `seenOrder` and `primaryOf`), the registry row in `packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts`, `content/docs/ui/pages.mdx`.

<details><summary>Local gates on 9b06321b</summary>

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint typecheck` and `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2`: VERDICT command-exit 0; Test Files 223 passed (223), Tests 9393 passed (9393) (taken on fdb041ae, before the docs-only transcript commit; no package source changed after it).
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` (derived on the branch, 100 commands, plus `pnpm check:doc-authoring` and `check-nul-bytes`): exit 0 on all but two, which are NOT MEASURED, not red:
  - `pnpm check:lean-entry-closure`: exit 3, PREREQUISITE NOT MET (loads built entry points of packages this container has not built; CI's run is the reading).
  - `node scripts/check-plugin-teardown-shape.mjs --self-test`: exit 3, its positive control is pinned to a commit this shallow clone cannot reach (CI's run is the reading).
- `pnpm check:docs-transcript-drift` was red on the first run (`react-pages.mdx:407` printed 74, the registry derives 75); fixed in 9b06321b and rerun: exit 0, 4 declared transcript values equal what the registry derives.
- Everything else, the eleven required contexts included, is read from this PR's check-runs.

</details>
